title: Selection of loss-of-function SPOP via yeast survival assay
methodText: Count matrices from two biological replicates were analyzed using DESeq2. Enrichment ratios between SPOP-expressed and non-expressed pools were quantified as z-scores, derived from the log2 fold-changes and their standard errors. Variant identification utilized both short-read (AVITI-seq) and long-read (Nanopore) sequencing; z-scores were calculated independently for each platform and combined using an inverse-variance weighted average.
abstractText: To comprehensively characterize the functional landscape of SPOP alteration, we performed a deep mutational screening (DMS), elucidating the functionality of 7,933 out of 8,228 possible single amino acid changes (96.4% coverage). Leveraging the observation that overexpression of human SPOP leads to yeast growth arrest, we assessed the functionality of each variant using a yeast proliferation assay.
shortDescription: An amino acid level deep mutational scan of human SPOP using yeast survival assay.

experiment.title: SPOP yeast growth inhibition
experiment.shortDescription: Deep Mutational Scan of the human SPOP using yeast growth inhibition reveals comprehensive functional landscape of variants.

experiment.methodText: DMS library was synthesized through tile-based cloning. We observed that expression of wild-type SPOP inhibits yeast growth, whereas depletion of specific functional regions within wild-type SPOP, namely the MATH, BTB, and 3-box domains, rescues it. To take advantage of the complementary strengths of both platforms, we analyze our mutant libraries using short-read and long-read sequencing.
